Hi Alejandra — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through Nimbus’s latency SLAs and the expected production profile. Quick recap and two asks so we can put together a clean private-offer sketch for procurement:

Recap (from our call)

- Peak: short bursts up to ~1.2B tokens in a month during reporting windows.
- Target unit economics: you asked whether we could hit ~$8-10 per 1M tokens on a private offer.
- Channel preference: AWS Marketplace private offer preferred (company policy + existing vendor flows).
- Procurement note: PO-based, single-line item preferred; Tom Lee is the procurement lead.

Asks
1) Can you confirm the 500M tokens/month baseline + procurement contact (Tom) — reply-all with any PO constraints?
2) Budget range you mentioned on the call: $8k-$12k/month — is that the committed monthly spend you can sign to a 3/6/12 month PO? Or is it more of a target run-rate?

What we’re going to do next
- Map target $/1M to AWS Marketplace SKU pricing (how private offers map to our per-1M token unit).
- Run sensitivity: given list PPU and likely marketplace fee stack, estimate the required commit to achieve $8/1M vs $10/1M.
- Share an initial rate-card + a one-page PO template for your legal/procurement to validate.

I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik internally to build the numbers. If Tom is available, we can set a short procurement sync later this week.

Thanks — Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + ask: marketplace private offer and target $/1M tokens

Connor — done a first pass and attached the calc sheet. Highlights / assumptions:

Assumptions
- Redwood list PPU for the referenced model: $20 per 1M tokens (list).
- AWS Marketplace surcharge & payments pipeline ~= 20% effective take-rate on top of our list when sold via standard marketplace flow (fees + billing adjustments).
- Private-offer discounts are primarily driven by commit size and contract term; we’ve historically seen 25-50% off list for 3-12 month private offers with a modest commit.

Sensitivity (rounded)
- No commit (month-to-month): list $20 + marketplace 20% = effective $24/1M => to hit customer target they need a >60% discount to reach $8/1M — unlikely without an enterprise commit.
- 6-month $50k commit: we can offer ~40% off list in private offer terms depending on model and capacity; calc: $20*(1-0.4)= $12/1M, plus marketplace fee becomes ~$14.4/1M effective to customer.
- To reach $8/1M effective, we'd need ~60% off list before marketplace fees (list * 0.4 = $8, then +20% market = $9.6). That implies a materially larger commit ($100k+ over term) or a special channel carve (rare).

Proposal for Nimbus
- Two-tier private offer: (A) 6-month $50k commit => private SKU priced at $12/1M (internal list discount 40%), displayed in the private offer. Customer invoice would show single-line PO for $50k committed, with monthly invoices applied to consumption. We provide a one-page appendix mapping $/1M for visibility.
- If they insist on $8/1M, propose $120k 6-month commit (or 12-month $200k) — I’ll flag this as high-risk and route to pricing leadership.

Ops note
- AWS marketplace wants line-item clarity. We can put the unit as "1M-token bundle SKU" so procurement sees $/1M transparency while invoices can also show committed dollar line. Internal metering will reconcile usage vs committed spend and we invoice the delta.

I attached redwood_marketplace_ppu_calc_v1.xlsx with the scenario tab filled (sheets: assumptions, scenario_summary, customer_view).

Marissa
Director, Cloud GTM | Redwood Inference
